subject: RStan: "hidden" reference objects in the global workspace

messages.author: 1718a05954397331
messages.subject: RStan: "hidden" reference objects in the global workspace
parts:
Dear Stan Users,

After a day of actively fitting a number of Stan models (with RStan 1.2.0), I've noticed that a number of "hidden" reference objects get stored in the global R workspace. They don't seem to take up much space by themselves, but they are "cumulative", i.e. re-writing the results of a fit over an existing variables will create a new "hidden" reference object. Here's what I have:

.__C__Rcpp_stan_fit4model33c2fe3f4e8_negbin_hierar   refClassRepresentation    61840    1      NA
.__C__Rcpp_stan_fit4model33c306e08d4_negbin_hierar   refClassRepresentation    61840    1      NA
.__C__Rcpp_stan_fit4model33c3091535d_negbin_hierar   refClassRepresentation    61840    1      NA

Presumably, these objects are related to the "save_dso" option used when compiling the Stan code, and are used to hold the contact point with the dynamically-loaded C++ code (is this a correct assumption?). My questions are as follows:
  • As I compile the same model (in the same .stan file) over and over during development and debugging, is there some "cleanup" of the previously-compiled libraries that is done in the Stan directories? I want to avoid old/buggy model object files polluting a compilation directory somewhere...
  • Do the above objects in the R environment hide references to much bigger data/code that would be saved, e.g. in the .RData file?
This applies to RStan 1.2, with R 2.15.2 on Mac OS X.

Many thanks for any help!
+ Nicolas

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] RStan: "hidden" reference objects in the global workspace
parts:
Good finding; may I ask how did you get that list?  In RStan, we do have to store the pointer to the "dynamic shared object" compiled from the model.  This is to avoid 'segfault' that would otherwise appear sometime. 

Could you just call gc() to remove those hidden objects?  I think that should work if all objects related to one model is not referred to in a R session.

Jiqiang

parts: Thanks for your quick answer Jiqiang. Answers to your questions below.

On Monday, March 18, 2013 11:17:32 PM UTC-4, Jiqiang Guo wrote:
Good finding; may I ask how did you get that list?  In RStan, we do have to store the pointer to the "dynamic shared object" compiled from the model.  This is to avoid 'segfault' that would otherwise appear sometime. 

Could you just call gc() to remove those hidden objects?  I think that should work if all objects related to one model is not referred to in a R session.

No gc() does not work since these objects do have an active reference from the global environment.  To get this list, I just use a standard R command:

ls(all.names=TRUE)

chained into a call to object.size() to get the size that R thinks the object is. The problem with object.size() is that it does not properly follow all references, so an object may be actually much bigger than its reported size is. (see below)

messages.author: ab7b24da45678eac
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] RStan: "hidden" reference objects in the global workspace
parts:
Thanks.  I saw the hidden R objects now, which are created by Rcpp in fact.  I do not know how/whether RCpp manages them.  RStan itself does not created any hidden objects.  The temporary file (dynamic shared object compiled from C++ code) can be seen for example as follows.

> acode <- 'parameters { real y;} model {y ~ normal(0,1);}'
> fit <- stan(model_code = acode)
.....
> get_stanmodel(fit)@dso
S4 class cxxdso: dso_saved = TRUE, dso_filename = file1b796de5b88b, size = 1.4 Mb.
And dso_last_path = '/var/folders/1x/sqww6q215t71967mr8ph987m0000gn/T//RtmpsrHs9Z/file1b796de5b88b.so'.
Created on: 'x86_64, darwin9.8.0' with 'CXXFLAGS =  -O3 $(LTO)     #set_by_rstan'.
Loaded now: YES.
The signatures is/are as follows:
$file1b796de5b88b
character(0)

For now, these files get created by RCpp, over which we do not have control.  We need to investigate if this is really annoying.  However, if we have a stanfit object say named fit and after I do the following

> fit <- stan(...)
> rm("fit")
> gc()
> getLoadedDLLs()

I could see that the compiled code were unloaded (i.e., not showing up from getLoadedDLLs).  So in the case, if we save the session, I do not think the hidden objects would refer to any object that is big.  Thus .RData file is not big. 


Jiqiang
